newsitem.title: UK: S&P raises Universal Outdoor Holdings to B plus.
newsitem.headline: S&P raises Universal Outdoor Holdings to B plus.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it raised its corporate credit ratings on Universal Outdoor Holdings Inc and its unit Universal Outdoor Inc, to B plus from B.
Additionally, Standard & Poor's said in a statement it raised its ratings on Universal Outdoor Inc's $65 million 11 percent senior notes due 2003 to B from B minus.
The agency said it raised Universal Outdoor Holdings' $50 million 14 percent senior secured discount notes due 2004 to B minus from CCC plus.
"These ratings are removed from CreditWatch, where they were placed June 19, 1996," S&P said in a statement.
Also, S&P assigned its B minus rating to Universal Outdoor Inc's planned $200 million senior subordinated notes due 2006.
The ratings outlook is stable, S&P said.
The higher ratings of this outdoor advertising company reflect a significantly larger pro forma sales base and greater geographic diversity as a result of acquisitions, S&P said.

"In addition, the overall financial profile is substantially strengthened, reflecting Universal Outdoor Holdings' July 1996 initial public offering (IPO) and the planned 5 million common share offering being sold in conjunction with the subordinated notes," the agency said.
S&P said financial measures improve substantially with the $62 million in net proceeds generated from the IPO and the planned common stock financing.
S&P said the ratings reflected Universal Outdoor's still heavy debt burden and related relatively weak overall financial profile, as well as the company's narrow business focus.
It said Universal Outdoor also faced significant integration challenges with the planned acquisitions, particularly in Florida because of its large size relative to the company's existing operations.
In addition, Standard & Poor's said it expected Universal Outdoor to continue to grow through largely debt financed acquisitions.
